text.p: The following are the reports carried by Estonia's newspapers on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:

- The administrator of bankrupt Oru peat plant in northeast Estonia was delivering 600,000 kroons in pay to workers when he received a phone call, ordering him to throw the money onto the road, otherwise a bomb would be detonated in his vehicle. The money was lost.

- Turkey and Estonia signed a free trade deal and an investment protection agreement. Visiting Turkish President Suleyman Demirel expressed the hope that Estonia and Turkey would both become European Union members.
- Banning abortion would increase the number of deaths due to illegal abortions, a member of the Family Planning Centre said after a protest march by the anti-abortion Union of Life.
- A court decision which said journalist Eino Tammer was guilty under the criminal code for asking questions about public figures was against international norms, the Broadcasting Union said.

- Observers predict war will break out again in the breakaway Georgian region of Abkhazia again. The Estonian foreign ministry admits there are problems in evacuating 300 ethnic Estonians from two Estonian villages in the area.
- 57 parliament members supported plans to erect a Liberty monument in a central Tallinn square.
- United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) will provide two million kroons for a project preparing a strategy for fighting poverty in Estonia.
- Estonia's chances to get in the European Union among the first new members were good, the Spanish Secretary of State on EU affairs told visiting Estonian Foreign Minister Toomas Ilves.
- A joint sea rescue exercise of Estonia, Russia, Finland and Sweden, simulating the collision of a tanker and a passenger ship, was successful, the chief of Estonia's border guard said.
- Thomson Bankwatch raised Estonia's rating from BBB- to BBB+, taking into account the development of the economy and reforms, a representative of Thomson said.
- The shares of clothes maker Baltika and ski maker Viisnurk will enter the main list of the stock exchange on Thursday.
